test_cases.test_name: Functional Test: X-bar/R Chart Creation and Nelson Rules Application
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can correctly create X-bar/R control charts from a CSV file and accurately apply the vendor's standard Nelson rules to identify out-of-control points.
prerequisites: SPC Dashboard software is installed and accessible
Test CSV file with at least 100 rows of sample QC data (subgroups with multiple measurements) is available
User account with 'Analyst' role permissions is configured

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using the pre-configured Analyst role credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful and the main dashboard interface is displayed.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the main dashboard screen post-login

test_steps.action: Navigate to the 'Import Data' section and select the pre-prepared test CSV file containing QC sample data.
test_steps.expected_result: CSV file is successfully uploaded and a confirmation message is displayed. Data preview is shown correctly.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the import confirmation message and data preview

test_steps.action: Select the option to create a new X-bar/R control chart, mapping the correct columns from the CSV as the measurement data and subgroup identifier.
test_steps.expected_result: X-bar and R charts are generated and displayed on the screen with calculated control limits (UCL, CL, LCL).
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the generated X-bar and R charts with visible control limits

test_steps.action: Enable the vendor's standard Nelson rules from the chart configuration or analysis menu.
test_steps.expected_result: Nelson rules are activated. The chart updates to highlight any data points that violate the enabled Nelson rules.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the chart showing highlighted points violating Nelson rules

test_steps.action: Manually verify the highlighted points against the expected rule violations by checking the source data and rule logic.
test_steps.expected_result: The points highlighted by the system correctly correspond to the expected violations of the Nelson rules as per the test data.
data_to_capture: Record of the verified rule violations and corresponding data points

acceptance_criteria: X-bar and R charts are generated successfully from the CSV input without errors.
Control limits (UCL, CL, LCL) are calculated and displayed correctly on the charts.
The vendor's standard Nelson rules are applied and correctly identify predefined out-of-control conditions in the test data.
The system response time for chart rendering after data import is less than 2 seconds.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 211.110 - Sampling and testing of in-process materials and drug products.
General principles of data integrity (ALCOA+) for accurate data representation.
data_integrity_requirements: The original data from the CSV must be accurately represented in the chart without alteration.
The application of Nelson rules must be consistent and reproducible.
urs_requirements: URS-020-001: Users shall create X-bar/R and p-charts from CSV inputs.
URS-020-002: Users shall apply vendor's standard Nelson rules.
URS-020-011: Render charts in < 2 seconds after filter changes.
required_expertise: Basic understanding of control charts and Nelson rules

test_cases.test_name: Integration and Security Test: Data Import and Role-Based Access
test_cases.objective: To verify the system's ability to import data via standard ODBC connection and enforce role-based view access controls as specified.
prerequisites: SPC Dashboard software is installed and accessible
A test database is available with a configured ODBC DSN
Two user accounts are configured: one with 'Admin' role and one with 'Viewer' role
A sample dataset is loaded into the test database

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using the pre-configured Admin role credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful and the main dashboard interface with full administrative menu is displayed.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the admin dashboard post-login

test_steps.action: Navigate to the data import section and select the ODBC connection option. Configure the connection using the pre-defined DSN to the test database.
test_steps.expected_result: ODBC connection is established successfully. A list of available tables/views from the test database is displayed.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the successful connection and table list

test_steps.action: Select a predefined table or view containing QC data and complete the import process.
test_steps.expected_result: Data is successfully imported from the ODBC source into the SPC dashboard. A confirmation message is shown.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the import confirmation and data preview

test_steps.action: Create a simple chart or report from the imported ODBC data and mark the dataset as 'Released' using the admin functionality.
test_steps.expected_result: Chart is created successfully. The dataset status is changed to 'Released' and the system confirms the action.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the released dataset status

test_steps.action: Log out of the Admin account and log in using the pre-configured Viewer role credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful, but the interface shows limited options compared to the Admin view.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the Viewer role dashboard highlighting limited menu options

test_steps.action: Attempt to access the chart created from the released ODBC dataset. Then attempt to edit the data or the chart configuration.
test_steps.expected_result: The Viewer can view the chart in a read-only mode. Any attempt to edit the data or configuration is prevented by the system (e.g., edit buttons are disabled or an access denied message appears).
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the chart in read-only mode and any access denial messages

acceptance_criteria: Data is successfully imported into the SPC dashboard from a configured ODBC source.
The Admin user can successfully mark a dataset as 'Released'.
The Viewer user has read-only access to the released dataset and cannot modify it.
The system correctly restricts menu options and functionality based on the user's role.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11.10 - Controls for closed systems, including user access controls.
URS-020-007: Read-only access for released datasets.
data_integrity_requirements: Data imported via ODBC must be a complete and accurate representation of the source data.
Access controls must be enforced to prevent unauthorized modification of released data.
urs_requirements: URS-020-004: The dashboard shall allow role-based view access.
URS-020-007: Read-only access for released datasets.
URS-020-012: Import data from CSV and ODBC connections using standard connectors.
URS-020-013: Integrate with AD for user authentication if supported by vendor.

test_cases.test_name: Performance Testing: Data Loading and Chart Rendering
test_cases.objective: Verify the system meets performance requirements for loading large datasets and rendering charts within specified time limits
prerequisites: System installed and configured
Test CSV file with 100,000 data points prepared
Stopwatch or timing tool available
User with appropriate permissions logged in

test_steps.action: Navigate to the data import section and select the CSV file containing 100,000 data points
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts the file and begins processing
data_to_capture: Time taken from file selection to completion of data loading

test_steps.action: Apply filter changes to the loaded dataset and initiate chart rendering
test_steps.expected_result: Charts are rendered with the filtered data
data_to_capture: Time taken from filter application to complete chart rendering

acceptance_criteria: Data loading completes in less than 5 seconds
Chart rendering completes in less than 2 seconds after filter changes
All data points are accurately represented in the charts
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records performance
GAMP 5 guidelines for performance verification
data_integrity_requirements: All 100,000 data points must be accurately loaded without corruption
Chart calculations must maintain data integrity throughout filtering operations

test_cases.objective: Verify the system's export capabilities to PDF/CSV formats and annotation functionality for data points
prerequisites: System installed and configured
Sample dataset loaded
User with appropriate permissions logged in
Email client configured for testing if applicable

test_steps.action: Create annotations on specific data points using the built-in comment feature
test_steps.expected_result: Annotations are successfully attached to the specified data points and visible on the chart

test_steps.action: Export the current chart view to PDF format using the vendor's standard export function
test_steps.expected_result: PDF file is generated containing the chart with annotations and data
data_to_capture: Inclusion of annotations in exported file

test_steps.action: Export the dataset to CSV format using the vendor's standard export function
test_steps.expected_result: CSV file is generated containing all data points and relevant metadata

acceptance_criteria: Annotations are properly saved and displayed with data points
PDF exports contain all chart elements including annotations
CSV exports contain complete and accurate data
Exported files are readable and properly formatted
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
EU Annex 11 for electronic data integrity
data_integrity_requirements: Exported data must match source data without alteration
Annotations must be permanently associated with correct data points
Export formats must maintain data structure and integrity

test_cases.test_name: Audit Trail Verification for Configuration Changes
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system maintains an audit trail for configuration changes as provided by the vendor, ensuring traceability and compliance.
prerequisites: System administrator access
Configured SPC dashboard with existing chart configurations
Vendor documentation on audit trail functionality

test_steps.action: Log in to the SPC dashboard with administrator credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: Successful login and access to administrative functions.

test_steps.action: Navigate to chart configuration settings and modify an existing configuration (e.g., change Nelson rule parameters).
test_steps.expected_result: Configuration changes are successfully saved.

test_steps.action: Access the audit trail log through the vendor-provided interface.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail log is accessible and displays entries.

test_steps.action: Verify the audit trail entry contains user, timestamp, and change details.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail entry accurately records the configuration change with all required metadata.

acceptance_criteria: All configuration changes are recorded in the audit trail
Audit trail entries contain user, timestamp, and change details
Audit trail is read-only and tamper-proof
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11
EU Annex 11
GMP data integrity principles
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail must be secure and immutable
All changes must be attributable to specific users
Complete record of configuration history must be maintained

test_cases.objective: Verify that the vendor scheduler correctly sends scheduled reports via email to designated recipients with proper attachments.
prerequisites: Configured email server settings
Active user accounts with email addresses
Pre-configured report templates
Scheduled report job setup

test_steps.action: Log in to the SPC dashboard with scheduling privileges.
test_steps.expected_result: Successful login and access to scheduling functions.

test_steps.action: Configure a scheduled report job with specific parameters (frequency, recipients, report type, format).
test_steps.expected_result: Scheduled job is successfully created and saved.

test_steps.action: Trigger the scheduled job manually or wait for scheduled time.
test_steps.expected_result: Job executes successfully without errors.

test_steps.action: Verify email delivery to all designated recipients.
test_steps.expected_result: Email is received by all configured recipients with correct attachments.

test_steps.action: Validate the report content matches the configured parameters.
test_steps.expected_result: Report content is accurate and complete per the scheduled configuration.

acceptance_criteria: Scheduled reports are delivered to all configured recipients
Reports contain correct data in specified format
Email system integrates properly with vendor scheduler
regulatory_basis: GMP reporting requirements
Data integrity principles for distributed reports
data_integrity_requirements: Reports must maintain data integrity during export and transmission
Email distribution must be secure and reliable

test_cases.test_name: Read-Only Access Verification for Released Datasets
test_cases.objective: To verify that once a dataset is marked as released, it can only be accessed in a read-only mode by all users, preventing any modifications.
prerequisites: User accounts with different roles (e.g., Viewer, Analyst, Admin) are configured
A test dataset has been imported and marked as 'released'
The system is running and accessible

test_steps.action: Log in to the SPC dashboard with an Analyst role account.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful, and the dashboard home screen is displayed.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the login screen and successful login

test_steps.action: Navigate to the list of datasets and select the dataset marked as 'released'.
test_steps.expected_result: The system opens the dataset for viewing. All editing functions (e.g., modify data, change chart parameters) are disabled or hidden.
data_to_capture: Screenshot showing the dataset view with disabled edit controls

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify a data point or a chart configuration associated with the released dataset.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents the modification and displays a message indicating the dataset is read-only.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the error message or system response

test_steps.action: Log out and log in with an Admin role account. Repeat steps 2 and 3.
test_steps.expected_result: Even with Admin privileges, the released dataset is accessible only in read-only mode. Modification attempts are prevented.
data_to_capture: Screenshot confirming Admin user also has read-only access

acceptance_criteria: Released datasets are accessible only in read-only mode for all user roles
Any attempt to modify a released dataset is prevented by the system with an appropriate message
The system behavior is consistent across different user roles
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 - § 11.10(e) - Protection of records to enable their accurate and ready retrieval throughout the records retention period.
EU Annex 11 - Clause 4.2 - For the storage of data it should be possible to retrieve current and obsolete data.
data_integrity_requirements: Data integrity for released records must be maintained by preventing alterations.
The system must enforce the read-only state consistently.
urs_requirements: URS-020-007: Read-only access for released datasets.

test_cases.test_name: Verification of Controlled Record Retention for Chart Configurations
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly retains and manages chart configurations as controlled records, ensuring they are preserved and cannot be unintentionally altered after creation.
prerequisites: User account with permissions to create and save chart configurations is available
A sample dataset is imported into the system
The system is running and accessible

test_steps.action: Log in to the SPC dashboard with a valid user account.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful, and the dashboard home screen is displayed.

test_steps.action: Create a new X-bar/R chart configuration using the imported sample dataset. Set specific parameters (e.g., subgroup size, control limits). Save the configuration with a unique name.
test_steps.expected_result: The chart configuration is saved successfully, and the system confirms the save action.

test_steps.action: Log out of the system and log back in. Navigate to the saved configurations and open the recently created chart configuration.
test_steps.expected_result: The chart configuration is retrieved and displayed exactly as originally saved, with all parameters intact.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the loaded configuration showing all parameters are correct

test_steps.action: Attempt to save a new configuration with the same name as the existing one.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents overwriting the existing configuration, either by requiring a new name or by creating a new version, as per vendor design.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the system's response to the save attempt

test_steps.action: If the vendor system supports versioning, check the version history for the saved configuration.
test_steps.expected_result: A history of the configuration is available, showing the initial creation event.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the version history, if applicable

acceptance_criteria: Chart configurations are saved and retained accurately by the system
Saved configurations can be reliably retrieved and display the correct parameters
The system has a mechanism to prevent accidental overwriting of existing configurations
Version history is maintained if supported by the vendor
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 - § 11.10(a) - Validation of systems to ensure accuracy, reliability, and consistent intended performance.
FDA 21 CFR Part 211 - § 211.68 - Required controls for automated equipment to assure that master production and control records are followed.
data_integrity_requirements: Configuration records must be maintained accurately to ensure the reproducibility and validity of statistical charts.
The integrity of the controlled record must be preserved from creation through its retention period.
urs_requirements: URS-020-008: Retain chart configurations as controlled records.
URS-020-009: Audit trail for configuration changes if provided by vendor.
